title: Touring with dancer May Elaine on the Orpheum Circuit
summary: An agent brought Garland's band to Chicago to back May Elaine, a white dancer in blackface who stepped out of a cotton bale, on the Orpheum Circuit for some months.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: When I left there, an agent come and got me to bring a band to Chicago, to play for May Elaine.
Uh-huh. And she was a singer.
She was a white girl, you know.
In blackface. And have a bale of cotton on the stage.
And when we came out and played the opening, this bale of cotton would open up.
And she'd step out of that and start to dance.
I see. And you worked with her -- did you travel on the Orpheum Circuit then?
I see. And how long did that happen, Tootie? How long did you do that?
Didn't stay there too long. Must have been a few months.
You know, when they'd go on vacation, or the theaters have a -- the actors have a vacation.
